premises.claim: The operator’s complete policy is not stated in the record.
The argument’s claim is explicitly conditional on a hypothetical policy that eschews using exposure as a means.
If a policy does not rely on exposing persons as a means, then there is no instrumental employment of those persons within that policy.

response.bridge: Under the interpretive assumption, the conditional form (“If policy P, then no instrumental employment”) is a valid statement even when the actual policy is unknown; the truth of the conditional does not depend on the antecedent being actual but on the logical connection asserted.
qualifications: The defended claim is purely hypothetical; nothing here establishes that the hypothetical policy is the actual policy in force.
response.strongest_conclusion: The statement “The absence of instrumental employment is conditional on that policy” is defensible as a hypothetical conditional; whether the antecedent policy holds in fact remains undetermined.
remaining_questions: What is the operator’s actual complete policy regarding gate operation and worker exposure?

claims.text: Suppose the operator pursues rescue without relying on exposure.
The proposed policy does not rely on exposing staff.
No person is employed through exposure in this proposed policy.
The absence of instrumental employment is conditional on that policy.

bridges.explanation: If the operator’s aim is rescue (goal) and the policy disavows relying on exposure (belief) so that no one is used through exposure (use), then, given the maxim, the absence of instrumental employment follows.
